record.summary: Priya Menon bought a 55‑inch smart TV for Rs 62,000 from an online marketplace during a festival sale, sold by a third‑party seller. The listing promised a 1‑year brand warranty and a 7‑day replacement. The TV arrived with a dented box but worked initially. After 20 days a vertical line appeared on the screen, and a week later the panel failed completely. She raised a complaint on the platform, which directed her to the seller. The seller claimed the damage was physical and not covered. The brand’s service centre sent a technician who, without opening the TV, marked the issue as customer‑induced damage and voided the warranty. Over six weeks Priya has been shuttled between the platform, seller and brand, receiving contradictory replies. She seeks a refund or replacement and compensation for the harassment, and wants to know who is legally liable and which forum to approach.
record.goal: Obtain a refund or replacement of the TV and compensation for the harassment, and determine the appropriate legal forum and responsible party.

Have you attempted to register the warranty on the brand’s website, and what was the result?
Do you have any written response from the seller or the platform that states their position, with dates attached?
contradictions: Seller claims the damage is physical and not covered, while Priya asserts it is a manufacturing defect appearing within warranty.
Brand’s technician marked the issue as customer damage without inspecting the device, contradicting the seller’s claim of physical damage.
Platform says it is only an intermediary, yet it directed Priya to the seller and promised the seller would resolve the issue.
evidence: Product listing screenshot showing "1-year brand warranty + 7-day replacement"
Unboxing video (delivery day) showing dented box and functional screen
Photos of vertical line on screen (Day 20)
Platform chat transcripts and email threads indicating referral to seller
Technician's service report stating "physical damage suspected, warranty void" without photographs

events.description: Priya placed an order for a 55‑inch smart TV priced at Rs 62,000 on an online marketplace during a festival sale, with a third‑party seller.
The TV was delivered; the box had a minor dent but the screen worked when first powered on. Priya recorded an unboxing video showing the dent and a functional screen.
A vertical line appeared on the TV screen.
The TV panel failed completely and stopped working.
Priya raised a complaint on the online platform; the platform directed her to the seller.
The seller responded that the panel damage was "physical" and therefore not covered under warranty or the 7‑day replacement.
The brand’s service centre sent a technician who, after a brief visit, marked the issue as "customer damage, warranty void" without opening the TV or providing photographs.
Priya spent six weeks on phone calls and chat sessions with the platform, seller and brand, receiving contradictory responses from each party.
